text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition and ruling socialist Party of Serbia supporters are to hold rallies at the same time Tuesday afternoon in the centre of Belgrade.
- Serbian patriarch Pavle calls on the two sides to refrain from parallel demonstrations in order to avoid possible confrontation.
- Serbian farmers, protesting over unpaid products, Monday blocked some roads in Serbia and announced a general blockade of roads and factories for Tuesday.
- Independent trade union Nezavisnost will organise workers' protests Tuesday at noon in front of the Serbian parliament building over the labour relations law that is to be passed today.
- Bankers forecast devaluation of the domestic currency during or immediately after the holiday season.
- Belgrade Catholic archbishop France Perko said the Pope Paul II could visit Sarajevo at the end of April at the earliest and he would invite him to visit Belgrade during this trip.
- Serbian parliament to adopt the republic's budget Tuesday.

- Petrol and diesel fuel prices went up by 50 paras per litre from midnight Monday according to the new Serbian government regulation under which the additional funds will be used for building of roads.
- Agriculture committee of the Serbian parliament calls for controlled imports of meat and dairy products.
- A meeting to be held in the National Bank of Yugoslavia Wednesday to find ways to pay farmers for their sugarbeet, sunflower and soybean, says Yugoslav agriculture minister Tihomir Vrebalov.
- Real wages in Yugoslavia went up by 17 percent in 1996, says federal statistics office.
- Rallies of support to President Slobodan Milosevic held in a number of towns in Serbia - Kraljevo, Kosovo Polje, Velika Plana.

- Yugoslav United Left (JUL) coalition partner of the ruling Socialist party of Serbia, held meetings of support to the policy of president Slobodan Milosevic in all 188 municipalities where it is active.
